Theme

Latin word

quāpropter

why? what for?; as a relative, and that is why

In this lexicon

  • why

    also used · classical · Plaut. Asin. 630b: Quāpropter, quaesō?; Plaut. Most. 208b: Quāpropter?

Notes

  1. 1quāpropter: long a (Lewis & Short’s headword quă-propter). It is the ablative quā with propter after it, as the tmesis shows: quā mē propter addūxī (Ter. Hec. 3.3.4, as Lewis & Short cites it). Lewis & Short writes quā-rē for the same ablative, and in its own article prints Quāpropter? where it quotes Plaut. Most. 3.2.140.

Examples

  • Quāpropter, quaesō? — Quia ego hanc amō et haec mē amat.

    Why, may I ask? — Because I love her and she loves me.Plaut. Asin. 630b–631
